title: The Moment Between
hook: You know the model. So why do you still break it?

launchpad.outcome: Notice the gap between seeing the chart and placing the trade, and learn the PAUSE that lives there.
launchpad.missionQuestion: Did price change, or did my emotion change?

slides.headline: You already know the rules, so why do you still break them?
slides.line: Phases 1–6 taught you how to read the market. Now you’ll learn how to read yourself while you trade.

slides.headline: One red candle shows up, and your plan is still the same.
slides.line: You’re in a valid long trade. Your stop loss is 30 points below, and your target is 60 points above.

check.prompt: So what actually changed in this moment?

options.label: The chart changed on me
options.feedback: It was one normal pullback. Your stop loss and your target didn’t move at all.

options.label: Something changed inside me
options.feedback: Exactly. The plan didn’t change. You did.

slides.headline: Every trade is decided in the gap between seeing and doing.

cards.label: Phases 1–6
cards.sub: You learned how to read the market.

cards.label: Phase 7
cards.sub: You learn to read yourself while you read the chart.

check.prompt: Which one makes you break more of your rules?

options.label: Not knowing the chart well enough
options.feedback: You already know the chart. That usually isn’t where things go wrong.

options.label: A feeling taking over my decision
options.feedback: Yes. Catching a feeling before it takes over is exactly what Phase 7 trains.

slides.line: Phases 1–6 trained your eyes on the chart. Phase 7 trains what happens inside you before you click.

slides.headline: First you feel it, and then you choose.
slides.line: This is your new routine for every trade. Tap each step to see what it looks like.

steps.label: Feel
steps.sub: A feeling shows up while you’re in a trade.

steps.label: Notice
steps.sub: You catch yourself in the middle of feeling it.

steps.label: Name it
steps.sub: You call it what it is: fear, greed, or FOMO (fear of missing out).

steps.label: Check the rule
steps.sub: You ask yourself, “What does my plan say here?”

steps.label: Choose
steps.sub: You act on the plan, not on the feeling.

slides.headline: ⏸ Before you enter or exit, hit PAUSE first.
slides.line: Pausing means you check four things before you act: the market, your plan, your mind, and your action. Tap each one.

steps.label: Market
steps.sub: It’s a normal pullback, and nothing important has changed.

steps.label: Plan
steps.sub: No rule was triggered, so you hold to your stop or target.

steps.label: Mind
steps.sub: You feel nervous, and you just want that feeling to stop.

steps.label: Action
steps.sub: Nothing needs to change, so you stay in the trade.

slides.quote: Fear doesn’t have to leave the room. It just doesn’t get to hold the mouse.

slides.prompt: Think about the last trading rule you broke. What were you feeling right before you broke it?
slides.modelAnswer: I knew the rule. Right before I broke it I felt something (rushed, scared, excited) and the feeling made the decision instead of the plan.

takeaways: Feel it. Notice it. Name it.
Check the rule before you act.
Did price change, or did I?
remember: YOU DON’T HAVE TO CONTROL EVERY FEELING. YOU HAVE TO CONTROL WHAT IT GETS TO CHANGE.
